title: Psalm 131: Like a Weaned Child
summary: In three short verses the psalmist tells the LORD that his heart is not proud and his eyes not haughty, and that he does not reach for things too great for him. He has calmed and quieted his soul, like a weaned child resting with its mother. Then he turns to the whole people: Israel, hope in the LORD, now and forever.

line: Three verses: a heart that is not proud, a soul calmed and quieted like a weaned child with its mother, and a call for Israel to hope in the LORD.
guide: Set down some of the questions too big for you, and some of the ambitions you have been grabbing at. The psalm does not say they do not matter; it says you can be quiet with God while they wait.

stanzas.title: Not proud, not reaching for things too great
A quieted soul, like a weaned child with its mother
Israel, hope in the LORD forever

verses.t: A song of ascents. Of David. My heart is not proud, O LORD, my eyes are not haughty. I do not aspire to great things or matters too lofty for me.
Surely I have stilled and quieted my soul; like a weaned child with his mother, like a weaned child is my soul within me.
O Israel, put your hope in the LORD, both now and forevermore.
